rationales: Mastication is the grinding and chewing of food by the teeth.
Lubrication moistens food, mainly through saliva.
Absorption is the uptake of digested nutrients.
Defecation is the elimination of feces.
Margulis did not introduce the five-kingdom classification system.
E. Chatton proposed the terms prokaryote and eukaryote.
Carolus Linnaeus developed an influential classification system but not the five-kingdom system.
Robert Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification system.
Protein synthesis occurs mainly at ribosomes, not as the chloroplast’s principal function.
DNA replication can occur in chloroplasts, but it is not their principal function.
Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.
ATP synthesis occurs during photosynthesis, but photosynthesis is the chloroplast’s overall function.
Chiasmata form during prophase I as homologous chromosomes undergo crossing over.
Telophase I occurs after chiasmata have formed and homologous chromosomes have separated.
Metaphase I follows the formation of chiasmata.
Anaphase I separates homologous chromosomes after chiasmata have formed.
Karl Lohmann discovered ATP in 1929.
Calvin is known for research on photosynthesis, not the discovery of ATP.
Hans Krebs is known for the Krebs cycle, not the discovery of ATP.
Emil Fischer is known for work on sugars and enzymes, not the discovery of ATP.
Albumin helps maintain osmotic pressure but is not the blood-clotting protein asked for.
Globulins include various transport and immune proteins, not the principal clotting precursor.
Hemoglobin transports oxygen in red blood cells.
Fibrinogen is converted into fibrin during blood clotting.
Dr. Abdul Salam is associated with the saying that scientific knowledge is the common heritage of mankind.
Dr. Atta ur Rehman is not the person associated with this saying.
Dr. Samar Mubarak is not the person associated with this saying.
Dr. Abdul Qadeer is not the person associated with this saying.
The study of fishes is ichthyology.
The study of mammals is mammalogy.
The study of birds is ornithology.
The study of insects is entomology.
Observations are recorded evidence, not the logical consequences of a hypothesis.
Deduction is the reasoning used to derive logical consequences from hypotheses.
Summarization condenses information rather than deriving consequences from hypotheses.
Experiments test hypotheses and their predictions rather than being the logical consequences themselves.
Folic acid is converted into tetrahydrofolate, which functions as a coenzyme, so this is also a valid choice.
Glycerine is not a vitamin and does not act as a coenzyme.
Riboflavin gives rise to the coenzymes FMN and FAD, making this a valid choice too.
Glucose is a sugar, not a vitamin or coenzyme; the question is ambiguous because both folic acid and riboflavin are valid.
The cell wall provides structural support and does not construct ribosomes.
The nucleolus is where ribosomal components are made and assembled.
The endoplasmic reticulum can bear ribosomes but does not construct them.
Plastids have their own ribosomes but are not the site where the cell’s ribosomes are constructed.
Crossing over is the exchange of segments, not the point where chromatids remain attached.
A bivalent is a pair of homologous chromosomes, not the attachment point between chromatids.
A chiasma is the point where non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes remain connected after crossing over.
Metaphase is a stage of cell division, not a point of chromatid attachment.
Chromatin is the loose, thread-like form of genetic material in the nucleus.
The centromere is the region joining sister chromatids.
Spindle fibers help move chromosomes during cell division.
The nucleolus is a nuclear region involved in ribosome production.
Calvin did not first use the term enzyme.
Wilhelm Kühne first used the term enzyme.
Fischer is known for the lock-and-key model of enzyme action, not for coining the term.
Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model, not the term enzyme.
Chlorophyll b is an accessory pigment rather than the main photosynthetic pigment.
Carotenoids are accessory pigments that absorb additional wavelengths.
Chlorophyll a is the principal photosynthetic pigment.
Chlorophyll c is an accessory pigment found in some groups of algae.
